title: Miao's majorisation conjecture for concave singular-value functions
statement:
Let $X,Y\in\mathbb{M}_{n,m}(\mathbb{C})$, and let $\sigma_i(X)$ denote the singular values in non-increasing order. Let $f:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+$ be concave with $f(0)=0$. **Miao's conjecture.** For every $k\leq n,m$,

$$
\sum_{i=1}^k\left|f(\sigma_i(X))-f(\sigma_i(Y))\right|\leq\sum_{i=1}^k f(\sigma_i(X-Y)).
$$

This strengthens the one-sided majorisation inequality stated immediately before it; the source attributes the conjecture to W. Miao and gives no resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.5232

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2012).
source_name: K. M. R. Audenaert and F. Kittaneh, “Problems and Conjectures in Matrix and Operator Inequalities”, arXiv:1201.5232 (2012).
